terms.grammar: parenthesis: ut with the third person of videor
evidence: Plaut. Am. 333: Hinc enim mihi dextra vōx aurīs, ut vidētur, verberat.
Ter. Hec. 272b: Nunc quidem ut vidētur
terms.comment: Set into the sentence like English “apparently”, without changing its construction; ut mihi vidētur is “as I see it”. For one’s own guess, ut opīnor (see think).

terms.gloss: seem, appear (to be or to do)
terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, passive, with a nominative and infinitive
terms.comment: Latin turns the adverb into the verb: “apparently he is ill” is aeger esse vidētur, “he seems to be ill” (see seem).

phrases.latin: Certumne est istuc? — Nunc quidem ut vidētur.
phrases.english: Is that settled, then? — For now, apparently.

phrases.latin: Hinc enim mihi dextra vōx aurīs, ut vidētur, verberat.
phrases.english: Yes, a voice is beating on my ears from the right, apparently.
